title: Attention Is All You Need
notes: Annotated by hand. Most of this paper's headline results depend on scale and on WMT-size data, so the testable claims are the Table 3 ablations, which are internal comparisons of the same architecture.

claims.text: The Transformer reaches a higher BLEU score than previous best models, including ensembles, on WMT 2014 English-to-German.
claims.notes: One arm is an external published system that cannot be rerun, and the result depends on WMT-scale data.

claims.text: The big Transformer model achieves 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-German.
The big Transformer model achieves 41.8 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-French.
Single-head attention is worse than multi-head attention when the total computation is held constant.
claims.notes: An internal ablation on a small sequence task; the mechanism is not scale dependent.

claims.text: Too many attention heads also hurts quality, so there is an intermediate optimum.
claims.notes: The differences between 8, 16 and 32 heads are small; at reduced scale with three seeds this is likely inside the noise.

claims.text: Reducing the attention key size from 64 to 16 hurts translation quality.
claims.notes: A capacity ablation, visible on a small task.

claims.text: Learned positional embeddings perform nearly identically to sinusoidal positional encodings.
claims.notes: The paper itself reports near-identical results, so a correct reduced-scale run should find no difference, which is inconclusive rather than consistent.

claims.text: Dropout helps avoid overfitting in the Transformer.
claims.notes: Regularisation, which shows up readily at small scale.

claims.text: A four-layer Transformer reaches 92.7 F1 on WSJ section 23 constituency parsing in a semi-supervised setting.
claims.notes: A headline number on a dataset that is not freely bundled.

claims.text: The Transformer trains in significantly less time than recurrent or convolutional models of comparable quality.
claims.notes: A wall-clock claim about GPU-scale training; the comparison does not transfer to a CPU budget.
